content: The protein known as CENTG2, or Arf-GAP with GTPase, ANK repeat, and PH domain-containing protein 1, is an enzyme in humans encoded by the AGAP1 gene. HACNS1 is located within an intron of the CENTG2 gene, which is also referred to as Human Accelerated Region 2. HACNS1 is hypothesized to function as a gene enhancer that may have played a role in the evolution of the uniquely opposable human thumb. Additionally, it is suggested that HACNS1 may have contributed to modifications in the ankle or foot, enabling humans to walk upright on two legs. Current evidence indicates that among the approximately 110,000 gene enhancer sequences identified in the human genome, HACNS1 has undergone the most significant evolutionary changes since the divergence of humans from the common ancestors shared with chimpanzees. Model organisms have been employed to investigate the function of the AGAP1 gene. A conditional knockout mouse line, named Agap1tm1a(EUCOMM)Wtsi, was developed at the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute. Both male and female mice from this line underwent a standardized phenotypic screening to assess the effects of AGAP1 gene deletion.
